newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to improve if trend support hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent to improve if trend support hold.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* With IPE Brent crude futures now north of trend resistance, odds on further upside must have shortened somewhat.
* A settlement above $18.35 on the weekly chart next Friday will break the seven month down trend giving room for further gains.

Friday's break above long term down trend resistance lead by NYMEX crude was read as bullish, but analysts remain cautious over further gains for IPE Brent on Monday, although they say sentiment will improve if the longer uptrend support remains intact.

"Last week a couple of technical patterns on spot (NYMEX crude) had a knock on effect on Brent," Said Peter Sceats, analyst at CharTech-MCS. He said the mini imperfect double bottom on the NYMEX crude spot chart at $18.98/99 from last Monday and Tuesday and the $19.39/40 gap-up from Tuesday to Wednesday set up a relatively strong close for both crudes.
Looking forward, Sceats said that with the price now above trend resistance, odds on further upside must have shortened somewhat but good trendline support underpinned the market.
"Take a line joining the key lows since $17.32 trough (June 11) and you'll see what we believe to be the key dynamic support marker at this time," Sceats said, looking at front month Brent.
"This trend line crosses the price action at $17.98 on Monday and rises by one cent a day".
He said that while the price is on the right side of this line the seven week uptrend looks ongoing.
"On the weekly chart a settlement above $18.35 resistance next Friday will break the seven month down trend and it would be natural to look for further upside action," Sceats added.
Al Graham at Elliott wave remained cautiously bearish, "Confidence is less now, but a door to under $17.68 remains open as long as $18.79 resistance holds," Graham said.
The upper and low trend lines form a mildly bearish expanding wedge pattern on the Brent spot continuation chart.
That starts with July 11's low of $17.32 and high $17.90 and passes through July 15's $17.80 low and July 17's $18.79 high respectively.
These parameters are still seen capping and underpinning the market.
IPE gas oil futures continued to hold above congested trendline support around $162.50-$163.
Prices made good headway peaking at $167.75 on Friday on the back of stronger crude but will need to break resistance around the $168 double top to go higher still, analysts said.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
